claims.statement: The standard of proof for every crate under crates/ is agreement with the upstream reference implementation rather than self-consistency, and the suites are split accordingly: roundtrip.rs / apply.rs / decode.rs / convert.rs exercise the crate alone, interop.rs runs the upstream binary as a child process, and where a reference cannot be run a pinned reference-made artifact or a generated vector file stands in for it.

Interop tests skip rather than fail when their reference binary is absent: each suite probes first and returns early after printing a note to stderr, so a green cargo test only proves no regression on what the machine could exercise. xso-rs resolves maxcso through $MAXCSO and then $PATH via common::maxcso_binary(); xdelta-rs probes with `xdelta3 -V`; xps-rs probes with `flips --version`.

CI's dependency step installs xdelta3 (with mame-tools) explicitly for the xdelta-rs comparison tests, but installs neither maxcso nor flips, so the xdelta-rs interop path executes on every run while the xso-rs and xps-rs interop tests always skip in CI and are a local responsibility.

xso-rs/tests/interop.rs proves mutual readability in both directions for CSO and ZSO at 2 KiB and 64 KiB blocks: xso_rs output is decompressed by maxcso back to the original image, and maxcso --format=cso1/--format=zso output is decompressed by xso_rs back to the original image.

same_bytes_as_maxcso_zlib_cso asserts our CSO is byte-identical to `maxcso --format=cso1 --only-zlib` at block sizes 2048 and 16384, and deliberately uses the pseudo-text write_text_iso fixture (256-word vocabulary with a squared frequency skew) because ties between equal-sized zlib trials make trial order observable; ZSO has no such test since maxcso cannot run LZ4 HC 16 itself.

gdi-rs establishes agreement without running gdidrop: tests/convert.rs pins the exact descriptor gdidrop wrote at port time (including the jump to sector 45000 caused by REM HIGH-DENSITY AREA and the skipped pregaps), requires a near-miss comment 'REM HIGH-DENSITY AREA (TOC)' not to trigger that jump, and requires a single-BIN set to produce the same layout and track bytes as its split equivalent.

nsz-rs's crypto acceptance gate is cross-language and generated: scripts/gen_vectors.py drives the actual Python nsz primitives (nsz.nut.aes128, nsz.nut.Keys) from $NSZ_SRC with Keys.crc32_checksum disabled, and emits the DO-NOT-EDIT file tests/common/vectors_gen.rs holding titlekek, key-area-key, title-key-unwrap, seekable-CTR (offsets 0..1048591), XTSN (sectors 0,1,2,255,256) and mul_alpha_le vectors that tests/vectors.rs asserts in both directions.

Because synthetic keys can never satisfy the CRC32 source checks, the suites build their Keys with Keys::from_str(text, false) from the generated sources plus a fixed header_key; key-length validation still applies, so a 15-byte titlekek_source is an error.

Fixtures are generated deterministically rather than shipped: seeded xorshift writers produce ISO, ROM-like and CUE/BIN data into a tempfile TempDir so a failure is reproducible from its seed, and the shapes are chosen for the codec (all-zero, high-redundancy, incompressible and counting sectors; every gdi sector distinct so a mis-dropped pregap shows). Committed fixtures exist only where a reference tool produced them - crates/xdelta-rs/tests/data and crates/xps-rs/tests/data, located through env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR") - and each crate's helpers live in tests/common/mod.rs with #![allow(dead_code)].

tests/common/mod.rs in nsz-rs constructs properly encrypted NCAs from scratch - header encrypted with XTSN under a fixed header_key, wrapped title keys in the four keyblock slots, CTR sections using the real per-section counter, a common ticket with the title key under titlekek 0, and a Meta NCA whose PFS0 holds a CNMT listing each content NCA's SHA-256 - which lets pipeline.rs assert exact decrypted plaintext, which sections were decrypted, and CNMT verification counts without shipping retail content.

Malformed input must error rather than panic: xdelta-rs/tests/decode.rs tries every truncation and a byte flipped at every position of a patch (only a panic or hang fails, since some flips land where nothing checks), xps-rs/tests/apply.rs does the same sampled at (len/500).max(1), and nsz-rs/tests/malformed.rs targets allocations sized by untrusted header fields (NCZSECTN 1<<40, i64::MAX, -1; NCZBLOCK with i32::MAX blocks; PFS0 with u32::MAX counts or a u64::MAX member offset).

The nsz-rs malformed suite also pins deliberate tolerance rather than rejection: a PFS0 whose string table is one byte with no terminator must still decompress, NCAs with no CNMT fail under strict verification but are reported unverified without it, and a container with no NCAs succeeds even under strict.

The progress contract is asserted per crate: xps_rs::apply and xdelta_rs::decode callbacks must sum to the patch size, xso_rs::compress to the ISO and xso_rs::decompress to the packed file, gdi_rs::convert to the BIN total matching gdi_rs::input_size including dropped pregaps, and nsz-rs adds progress_follows_compression_not_read_ahead, which runs a BKTR update NSP on a one-thread pool and requires every callback to stay under a quarter of the total so the BKTR read-ahead cannot make the bar jump.

Every crate tests the .part contract in the form its format allows: xso-rs and nsz-rs truncate a packed file so the decode fails mid-write and assert the pre-existing output still reads 'keep me', that no <output>.part survives, and that a later complete run does replace it; xdelta-rs and xps-rs use a one-bit-flipped source (WrongSource) and prove nothing was left behind by counting directory entries; gdi-rs blocks a track's .part with a directory to show a half-written set is neither committed nor over-cleaned.

nsz-rs/tests/pipeline.rs pins lazy key loading with a loader that panics if called: an NCA-free container compresses and decompresses with no keys at all, while an NCA-bearing one fails the run naming prod.keys and leaves the previously written NSZ byte-identical with no .part behind.

Slow conversions are #[ignore]d with a reason string, and xso-rs/tests/interop.rs's index_shift_round_trips is currently the only ignored test in the crates: it builds a sparse ~2 GiB image, asserts probe reports index_shift 1, round-trips it through xso_rs (and through maxcso when available), works in tempfile::tempdir_in(env!("CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR")) and compares a MiB at a time.

The documented way to run the ignored slow tests is `cargo test --release -p <crate> -- --ignored` (for xso-rs the 2 GiB case, about 35 s), while a plain `cargo test -p <crate>` skips both ignored tests and tests whose reference tool is missing.

The crates are executed as part of the workspace: `cargo test --workspace --features oxyromon/server` locally (or test.sh, which runs llvm-cov over two feature sets), and in CI the `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --features oxyromon/server --lcov` step is what actually runs them since clippy only lints test targets. The root package adds the cross-crate check tests/crates.rs, which requires the four copied src/bin/<cli>/ui.rs files to be byte-identical to xso-rs's.

Interop coverage is narrowed where the reference tool is buggy or where the crate diverges on purpose: xps-rs only asks Flips for --ips and --bps-delta because Flips 2.01 crashes creating linear BPS and shrinking IPS (those cases are hand-built in apply.rs), and the xdelta-rs loop over seven xdelta3 configurations accepts Error::Unsupported mentioning DJW for -S djw while panicking on any other failure.
